isinstance: Returns True when an object is an instance of a class or any of several types.
issubclass: Returns True when a class is a subclass of another class or any type in a tuple.
iter: Returns an iterator over an iterable, or repeatedly calls a callable until a sentinel.
len: Returns the number of items in a sequence or collection.
list: Creates a mutable ordered sequence, optionally copied from an iterable.
locals: Returns a mapping of local variable names to their current values.
map: Applies a function to each item of one or more iterables, yielding results lazily.
max: Returns the largest item in an iterable or the largest of two or more arguments.
memoryview: Creates a zero-copy view over a buffer-supporting object's binary data.
min: Returns the smallest item in an iterable or the smallest of two or more arguments.
next: Retrieves the next item from an iterator, with an optional default if exhausted.
object: The ultimate base class for all Python classes; returns a featureless instance.
oct: Converts an integer to an octal string prefixed with 0o.
open: Opens a file and returns a file object for reading, writing, or updating.
ord: Returns the Unicode code point for a one-character string, or a byte value for length-1 bytes.
pow: Raises base to exp, optionally modulo mod; supports efficient modular exponentiation.
print: Writes objects as text to a stream, separated by sep and terminated with end.
property: Defines managed attributes with getter, setter, deleter, and optional docstring.
